summary.headline: Sharda Motor Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 54% YoY to INR1,211.2 crore, with EBITDA up 24% to INR125.7 crore at a 10.4% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR1,211.2 crore (+54% YoY) and gross profit INR233.1 crore (+20%). Management introduced value-added sales growth as a disclosure metric, reporting +27% for Q2 and +18% for H1, but did not give absolute figures. PBT before exceptionals rose to INR131.2 crore from INR101.9 crore, and PAT was INR99.4 crore. Management said new lightweighting and emission programs are still in ramp-up, with startup costs weighing on gross profit, and that export revenue has not yet started.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR101.9 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Gross profit INR437 crore; EBITDA INR229 crore at 10.3% margin

financial_highlights.change: vs INR209.6 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Emission systems (core ICE)
segments.commentary: Growth is described as coming from the existing emission vertical, with value-added sales helped by WLTP-related orders. No segment-level numbers were given.

segments.name: Lightweighting
segments.commentary: New control arm programs have entered SOP and are ramping, and the lightweighting vertical contributed to value-added sales growth. Chakan-3 facility is ramping in line with customer schedules.

segments.name: Exports / global
segments.commentary: Export revenue has not started; management said it will contribute once the secured orders reach SOP. North American genset SOP is slated for Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 industry growth may moderate because Q3 FY26 was a strong base (GST-led recovery and festive season), though underlying demand remains healthy.

H2 FY27 growth to be supported by ramp-up of lightweighting control arm orders, additional control arm programs, temperature-controlled tubes and North American export programs; quarterly timing depends on customer schedules.
Gross profit growth lagged value-added sales growth due to startup costs of new programs, product mix and non-indexed commodities; management expects benefits to show as programs mature.
Customer ramp-ups typically take about 1.5 to 2 years to reach peak annual business value (management stated these values are peak).
Subframe wins would require new capex that follows the order; control arm programs will be delivered from existing facilities.
Dividend policy in place; buyback or other capital return options are a Board decision and were not committed.
capex_capacity: Chakan-3 lightweighting facility is ramping up in line with customer schedules.
Factory licence received for the new Uttarakhand plant; SOP remains on schedule (no date given in call).
North American genset manufacturer SOPs due in Q3 FY27; management said it is on track with no postponement signalled by the customer.
Premium two-wheeler emission order: SOP planned Q1 FY28, with controlled incremental investment mainly in product-specific tooling and development.
Control arm order from an emerging Indian PV maker: SOP planned Q4 FY28, using existing facilities.
Acquisitions under evaluation at different stages; no timeline given. Criteria are value accretion, technology fit, integration feasibility and ROCE.
demand_pricing: Industry Q2 FY27: production +18.6% YoY to 105.6 lakh units; domestic sales +18.2% to 83.9 lakh; exports +23.9% to 20.9 lakh; PV production +24.9% (utility vehicles +28.9%); CV production +33.9%; two-wheeler production +16.5%; three-wheeler production +24.2%.
FADA retail data: CNG, LPG, hybrids and EVs at 41.9% of PV retail in August 2026, ahead of petrol at 40.8%; September near parity (41% vs 41.2%).
Orders secured in H1 FY27 in strategic categories (premium 2W emissions, powertrain-agnostic lightweighting, global) total about $61.5 million lifetime business value.
Premium 2W emission order: about $8.1 million annual peak value and $40.4 million lifetime value.
Lightweighting control arm order: about $3.9 million annual and $19.5 million lifetime value, won with Donghee's technology and licensing partnership.
Export orders announced total about $17.8 million peak annual value and about $94 million lifetime value.
Non-indexed commodities (consumables, BOPs, inbound freight) and product mix weighed on gross profit in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How is value-added sales calculated and what is its absolute value, and why does it grow faster than gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give absolute value-added numbers yet and said it is still working on them. The gap versus gross profit (27% vs 20%) reflects startup costs in new lightweighting programs, product mix and non-indexed commodities.

qa_highlights.question: Are the North American genset SOPs on schedule and linked to US EPA norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SOP for the North American genset orders is on track for Q3 FY27 with no postponement requested, and that one order may be linked to norms.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lightweighting business only stamping, and what is the Donghee role?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said control arms need high-tensile steel stamping plus design, process and assembly competence; Donghee contributes product and process technology.

qa_highlights.question: What is the WLTP impact on content per vehicle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the content impact of WLTP is marginal; BS7 could raise emission content more significantly once final norms are set.

qa_highlights.question: Are there acquisition timelines, and would a buyback be considered?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline was given for acquisitions. On buyback, management referred to the public dividend policy and said the Board will decide and declare any buyback in due course.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sharda won subframe business and what capex follows?
qa_highlights.answer: Control arm win is already secured; subframe RFQs are under business development. Subframe capex would follow an order, with the facility built within the delivery timeline.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth (+20%) trailing value-added sales growth (+27%): margin pressure from ramp-up startup costs and non-indexed commodities.
Export revenue has not yet started; the $17.8 million peak-value export orders depend on SOPs (North American genset in Q3 FY27).
Q3 FY27 industry growth may slow against a high Q3 FY26 base.
Global trade policy, tariffs and EPA-related timing uncertainty affect export programs.
Acquisition pipeline has no timeline; cash deployment between M&A and capital returns is undecided.
Catalyst pass-through revenue is not disclosed, which limits visibility into underlying growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order wins and demand, but cautious on near-term margins and tight on numbers. Management withheld absolute value-added sales, catalyst pass-through and buyback details, and used "we are on track" language for SOPs.
key_quotes: What is important to note is not only the order value, but the widening participation across customer segments and applications.
This has not translated into the similar growth in gross profit because these new programs are still at ramp-up stage, at startup stage, and there are associated startup costs as well.
There is no indication or no requirement of postponement as of now from the customer.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management held a 'stable outlook' and gave qualitative H2 FY27 support from lightweighting control arm ramp, new programs and North American export SOPs in Q3 FY27, backed by about $61.5M of H1 orders but with no quantified growth target.

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 54% YoY to INR1,211.2 crore, but the brief gives no split between volume, price and mix for revenue (value-added sales +27% has no absolute figure), and it names no one-off items, so the quality of growth cannot be confirmed from the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross profit grew +20% vs value-added sales +27% in Q2 and EBITDA margin was 10.4%; management expects startup costs and non-indexed commodities to ease as programs mature, but 1.5-2 years to peak, so benefit is uncertain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Chakan-3 is ramping, North American genset SOP is due Q3 FY27 and premium 2W emission SOP is planned Q1 FY28, with Uttarakhand plant licensed but undated; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% to INR2,222.3 crore and about $61.5M of H1 orders (premium 2W, lightweighting, global) ramp in H2, though Q3 faces a strong base and export revenue has not started.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Subframe wins would trigger new capex only after an order, and acquisitions are under evaluation with no timeline; utilisation not disclosed so no capacity-driven announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management held a 'stable outlook' and flagged a tougher Q3 FY27 industry comparison against a strong Q3 FY26 base.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged that Q3 FY27 industry growth may moderate against a strong Q3 FY26 base, and gross profit growth (+20%) is trailing value-added sales growth (+27%).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: North American genset SOP in Q3 FY27, premium 2W emission SOP in Q1 FY28 and Indian PV control arm SOP in Q4 FY28, all with secured orders.

rows.label: H1 FY27 strategic orders of about $61.5M lifetime value
rows.why: Orders include premium 2W emission ($40.4M lifetime, $8.1M annual peak) and lightweighting control arm ($19.5M lifetime), which convert as SOPs occur over the next 1.5-2 years.

rows.label: Export revenue start via North American genset SOP
rows.why: Export orders total about $17.8M peak annual and $94M lifetime value, and export revenue has not yet started; management says SOP is on track with no postponement requested, though tariffs and EPA timing add risk.
